commit_message:
* src/truetype/ttinterp.c (Ins_SHZ): Fix the range limit.

Fixes #1419 and #1420, as well as
    https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/499455833

findings.title: Unsigned integer underflow in Ins_SHZ limit calculation
findings.message: In Ins_SHZ, when the zone pointer gep2 selects zone 1 (the glyph zone), the loop limit is computed as `exc->zp2.n_points - 4U` to exclude phantom points. Because both operands are unsigned, if `exc->zp2.n_points` is less than 4 (i.e., 0, 1, 2, or 3), the subtraction wraps around to a very large unsigned value. The subsequent loop `for (i = 0; i < limit; i++)` then iterates far beyond the actual array boundary of `exc->zp2.cur`, causing out-of-bounds memory reads and writes via `Move_Zp2_Point`.
findings.suggestion: Before subtracting 4 from `exc->zp2.n_points`, guard the operation with a check that `n_points > 4U`. If the count is 4 or fewer there are no real points to shift and the function should return early.

ground_truth.root_cause: The introducing commit (1803559c) replaced a prior bounds check (`exc->zp2.n_contours > 0` + contours array lookup) with a simpler but unchecked unsigned subtraction `exc->zp2.n_points - 4U`. Because `n_points` is an unsigned type, no negative result is possible; instead, underflow silently produces a huge positive limit.
